messages:
Maya (CS): Quick summary from today's SummitHealth onboarding call — they had a handful of asks that feel product-y and could impact renewal if we don't show progress. Main points: per-account inference cost dashboard export (daily CSV), per-session transcript export for audits (PII-redaction option), and better retry behavior for transient GPU OOMs so long-running jobs don't fail silently. They explicitly tied next renewal to visibility into spend for pilot workloads.

Ethan (AE): they said: 'If we can't show cost per project by next quarter, we'll pause expansion.' Customer is migrating 3 internal teams to Redwood and is sensitive to multi-tenant billing clarity.

Ashwin (PM): Thanks — can you spell out which of the three is highest priority for them? Also any example of desired CSV layout or a compliance requirement for the transcript export?

Maya (CS): Priority order from the call: 1) daily per-account export (must include route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, timestamp, project_id) 2) session transcript export with ability to mask PII fields before export 3) retry policy for OOMs (configurable backoff + failover to smaller model). They mentioned they want an automated S3 push for the CSV. Example line they asked for: `2026-03-18,project-alpha,route:generate,redwood-m-1,intokens:432,outtokens:289,cost_usd:0.23`

Jordan (SE): Quick notes on feasibility: we already expose usage per-route in the console, but there's no first-class automated daily CSV export. Workaround: customers can call the usage API and run their own exporter. Example curl they can use now:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage?start=2026-03-17&end=2026-03-18&group_by=route,project" 
```This gets them the raw data; then they can transform to CSV. PII redaction on transcripts is trickier because transcripts are currently ephemeral in logs and we only store minimal traces for debugging.

Olivia (Product): Proposed triage buckets so we can score and prioritize: A) Daily per-account CSV export + S3 sink (high impact, medium effort) B) Session transcript export with server-side redaction controls (high impact, high effort + compliance review) C) Retry/fallback policy for OOMs (medium impact, low-medium effort) D) Retention/visibility controls for session logs (compliance). Can CS upload the customer's sample CSV layout and any compliance docs? I'll add these to the feedback tracker and propose a P2 for A, P1 for B if legal says required. @Jordan can you own a spike for A + C?

feedback-bot: Feedback recorded: FB-4821 — "SummitHealth: daily cost export + session export + OOM retry". Link: https://feedback.internal/redwood/FB-4821

Ashwin (PM): Thanks. CS, please attach the sample CSV schema and a short user story (3-5 lines) we can put into the ticket. Tentative plan: Jordan spike (2w) -> design doc -> 3wk implementation for CSV export (if no major infra changes). Marking A as P2 until we validate legal for B.

Jordan (SE): I'll take the spike. Deliverables: 1) spike verifying existing usage endpoint coverage, 2) prototype S3 sink using our event pipeline, 3) short runbook for data residency concerns (they're EMEA). Expect initial notes by 2026-04-01. Known risk: S3 sink will need encryption/KMS tie-in for some enterprise customers.

Maya (CS): Great — I'll get the sample CSV (they've got a template) and the redaction/compliance ask from their security lead, and I'll drop them into FB-4821. SummitHealth will be happy to pilot early. :thumbsup: @Ashwin @Olivia @Jordan

Ethan (AE): Appreciate the quick turnaround team. I'll prep negotiation language for the renewal convo assuming we can commit to the spike + a pilot milestone.

Olivia (Product): Perfect. Once we have the sample CSV and security notes, I'll slot FB-4821 into next planning and share an ETA.
